method: Started from the brief's candidate list plus other large deals with poor pre-deal target returns (Anadarko, Allergan, Warner Bros. Discovery, Frontier, Time Warner, Nielsen, Dish, Catalent, Kenvue, Aetna, Monsanto, Express Scripts). For each target I pulled the definitive merger proxy or information statement (DEFM14A/DEFM14C) from the target's EDGAR submissions index and recorded the CEO row (plus other NEOs where notable) of the Item 402(t) golden parachute table, with every column it itemises and the sub-tables that split cash into severance and bonus. Severance is the Cash column when its parts are not each printed as a single figure; any component left out of a field is named in the notes and is included in the stated total. Exit words come from the target's closing 8-K (Item 5.02) where it names the officer, otherwise from the table's termination assumption. basis is 'estimated' for every 402(t) figure; Paramount's Bakish is 'actual' because the 2025 proxy states his actual termination payments (the change-in-control enhancement lapsed before the deal closed). Stock: the target's own cumulative TSR from its last 10-K performance-graph table, or where the 10-K graph was image-only or absent, the latest proxy pay-versus-performance table, using only windows that start and end inside the executive's tenure. Executives who stayed with the acquirer after closing (so the double-trigger parachute was not triggered by any disclosed exit) and deals that were never completed are listed under rejected. Reporting-owner CIKs come from EDGAR full-text search of the executives' Form 3/4 filings.
